content.text: {"grade":3,"complete":false,"main_gap":"The central finite-transversal lemma is false, so the claimed finite union of divisibility sets—and hence periodicity—has not been established.","errors":[{"description":"The asserted blocker fact is false. Let F_i={c,a_i,b_1,...,b_{i-1}}. These finite sets are pairwise intersecting, but B_n={a_1,...,a_n,b_n} are infinitely many distinct inclusion-minimal finite transversals.","quote":"If a family of finite sets is pairwise intersecting and has a member $C$ of size $r$, then it has only finitely many inclusion-minimal finite transversals."},{"description":"The infinite-branch argument illegitimately changes the branch by inserting c. Subsequent selected sets and pruning decisions depend on the altered node, so this does not show that the original branch contains a contracted node.","quote":"Insert $c$ at its first such occurrence. Until the next occurrence nothing changes; at that next occurrence the element selected there is dispensable"}],"notes":"The pairwise-intersection observation, characterization conditional on finitely many transversals, enumeration of S, and final periodic-residue argument are sound. However, the false lemma is the essential finiteness step and cannot be repaired locally."}
